newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes firmer, off highs as heat slips.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes firmer, off highs as heat slips.

text.p: IPE gas oil closed firmer on Monday but off its session highs as NYMEX heating oil slid despite perceived support from forecasts for colder U.S. temperatures.
April gas oil closed up $1.25 a tonne at $170.75, off a session high of $173.25.
"There was some pretty good buying around lunchtime, but NYMEX didn't really live up to our expectations," a dealer said.
NYMEX heating oil was expected to find more support from forecasts of a late-winter cold snap in the key Northeast U.S. market.

May Brent was trading nine cents down at $19.65 a barrel at 1804 GMT, after slipping off a high of $19.97 as sentiment grew more bearish. The contract breached a supportive gap on the continuation chart at $19.70-$19.76 a barrel.
"The market wanted to head back to $20, but volumes were weak and we fell off with (NYMEX crude)," said one broker.
The May Brent/gas oil crack spread firmed to $3.40 a barrel.
